new_alerts.volume_trend: rising — weekly volume jumped from ~1.2-1.6M shares (late Aug) to a 6.46M-share spike the week of Sept 8-11 on the CEO insider-buy news, and has stayed elevated (~1.6-2.8M/day) through the following two weeks versus the prior ~4-month base average of ~2M/day

signals.insider_buying: CEO and director Patrick Miles made an open-market CASH purchase of 115,000 shares on Sept 10, 2026 at a weighted average price of $8.81/share, worth $1,013,150 — explicitly a 'P - Purchase' transaction (not an option exercise, RSU vesting, or 10b5-1 plan sale), raising his direct stake to 5,893,551 shares. This followed a separate open-market purchase by independent director Keith Valentine of 135,000 shares at $7.38 (~$996,192) on May 11, 2026, during the post-earnings selloff. Confirmed independently across SEC EDGAR-sourced filings, StockTitan, MarketBeat, TradingView, secform4.com, and openinsider.com.
signals.institutional_buying: 66.35% institutional ownership. Multiple funds established new or meaningfully increased positions per Q2 2026 13F filings: California State Teachers Retirement System increased its stake 743.5% (to 1,245,358 shares, ~$10.77M); Paradigm Capital Management took a new $9.41M position (1,088,200 shares); Bank of New York Mellon took a new $3.09M position; FirstWave Capital Management took a new $1.24M position; Great Lakes Advisors took a new $2.42M position. Institutional investors bought a combined ~$349M in shares over the trailing 12 months versus ~$240M in institutional selling (some funds, e.g. Engineers Gate and Squarepoint, trimmed positions), for net institutional accumulation.
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings (reported Aug 4, 2026): revenue of $214M (+15% YoY, beat consensus by ~$2.3M), surgical revenue +17% YoY on 20% case volume growth and 24% net-new-surgeon growth, adjusted EBITDA of $36M (+53% YoY, 17% margin), positive free cash flow, and a raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to ~$140M (from $134M) while reaffirming ~$882M full-year revenue guidance.
CEO's $1.01M open-market share purchase on Sept 10, 2026 itself acted as a catalyst, coinciding with the stock's ~19.7% single-day jump on Sept 11 on above-average volume.
Company remains on track for its first GAAP-profitable year in 2026 per management commentary and sell-side coverage.

Multiple analyst price-target increases following Q2 results: UBS raised to $16 (Buy), TD Cowen raised to $13 (Buy), BMO Capital raised to $12 (Outperform); Stephens initiated Overweight at $15 in July 2026.
analyst_moves: Consensus rating: Moderate Buy/Buy from 14-15 covering analysts (13 Buy, 1 Hold, 1 Sell), average 12-month price target ~$17.40, implying roughly 70% upside from the current price.
UBS Group raised price target to $16 (Buy) on Aug 5, 2026; TD Cowen raised to $13 (Buy) on Aug 5, 2026; BMO Capital raised to $12 (Outperform) on Aug 5, 2026.

new_alerts.thesis: Alphatec is a spine-focused medtech company that plunged ~32% in May 2026 on a Q1 revenue miss tied to its smaller EOS imaging segment, then built a roughly 4-month stable base between $7.50-$9.80 as its much larger surgical-implant business kept growing double digits and profitability kept expanding (adjusted EBITDA +53% YoY in Q2, guidance raised to $140M). The stock has since broken out gradually from the base into the $10-10.60 range on rising volume, capped by a sharp CEO open-market cash purchase of $1.01M on Sept 10, 2026 — a genuine, well-documented insider conviction buy, not a compensation-driven transaction — which coincided with a ~20% one-day pop on outsized volume and has held since. This sits alongside net institutional accumulation in the latest 13F cycle (several funds taking new positions, one increasing its stake more than 7x) and a nearly unanimous sell-side Buy consensus with ~70% implied upside to the average price target. Market cap (~$1.5B) keeps it well within the small/mid-cap bias.
new_alerts.risks: The May 2026 EOS-segment miss and subsequent multiple securities-law-firm investigations/shareholder suits over the guidance cut remain an overhang, and Q3/Q4 execution against the raised full-year targets is unproven. The stock remains GAAP loss-making and down ~34% over the trailing year despite the recent recovery, so the base-breakout thesis is still relatively fresh (roughly two weeks old) and unconfirmed by a second catalyst. Revenue-per-case has been declining low-single-digits on mix/biologics-attachment headwinds, a factor to watch next earnings. Some institutional holders (Engineers Gate, Squarepoint) cut positions in the same period, so institutional buying is net-positive but not unanimous.

Sept 21, 2026: Space Force/NRO satellite-optics order described by the company as 'the most critical order' in its 25-year history, with plans for a $100M+ space-related backlog (still the most specific dollar figure disclosed; no incremental contract value details have been released since)
Zero negative catalyst has emerged across all three sessions since the Sept 21 order (Mon/Tue/Wed); no insider selling and no analyst downgrade identified

Goldman Sachs (analyst Evie Koslosky) raised PT to $225 from $210 on Sept 21, 2026, maintaining Buy — reconfirmed via Moomoo/Futu news coverage, a second independent source, consistent with the prior UBS $225 PT reported Sept 9
UBS (Dan Leonard) raised PT to $225 from $175 on Sept 9, 2026, maintaining Buy

Securities class-action lead-plaintiff deadline of Sept 28, 2026 is approaching, tied to previously-disclosed clinical-data allegations dating to the July 27, 2026 complaint — confirmed via multiple law-firm press releases (Morningstar/PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, Newmediawire); this is a known risk factor, not a new catalyst, and carries no score impact per screening rules

Sept 16, 2026: Redemption of all outstanding Series A Convertible Preferred Stock for $6M cash, eliminating dilution risk — confirmed via company press release (neonc.com) and StockTitan 8-K coverage; this is a genuinely new, non-insider catalyst not previously logged

Sept 22, 2026: Positive topline Phase 2a data for NEO100 in recurrent IDH1-mutant high-grade glioma — six-month progression-free survival of 48.9% vs. a 20% prespecified benchmark (p=0.0047), median overall survival of 26.09 months; company plans to seek a Type B FDA meeting on a registrational pathway — confirmed via company press release and independent StockTitan/GlobeNewswire coverage; genuinely new, non-insider catalyst

Q2 2026 earnings (reported Aug 4, 2026): revenue of $214M (+15% YoY, beat consensus by ~$2.3M), surgical revenue +17% YoY on 20% case volume growth and 24% net-new-surgeon growth, adjusted EBITDA of $36M (+53% YoY, 17% margin), positive free cash flow, and a raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to ~$140M (from $134M) while reaffirming ~$882M full-year revenue guidance.
CEO's $1.01M open-market share purchase on Sept 10, 2026 itself acted as a catalyst, coinciding with the stock's ~19.7% single-day jump on Sept 11 on above-average volume.
~2-week-old catalyst remains the most recent: additional $20M investment in XTEND AI Robotics announced Sept 9, 2026, bringing total investment to $27.5M -- no incremental developments on this since

No new catalyst or insider signal emerged Wednesday or in pre-market Thursday; the decline appears to be continued give-back of the post-XTEND-announcement run-up rather than a company-specific negative event
Sept 8, 2026: Strategic collaboration with FANUC America to integrate Palladyne's physical-AI software with FANUC's industrial robot portfolio
Aug 26, 2026: SwarmOS integration partnership with NORDA Dynamics (combat-proven Underdog Autonomy Module)

Iridium Communications shareholder special meeting held today, Sept 24, 2026 at 8:30am ET to approve the ~$8B Rocket Lab/Iridium merger (record date Aug 21); board unanimously recommends approval -- a genuine new near-term catalyst confirmed via SEC EDGAR proxy filings and Iridium's DEFM14A

Iridium acquisition now fully financed after completion of a $1.944B at-the-market equity offering (announced Sept 15, reiterated Sept 22-23), removing the dilution overhang that had weighed on the stock
Space Force IDIQ and backlog strength remain the core thesis anchors, unchanged from prior runs
Guggenheim's Sept 14-15 Neutral initiation remains a mild overhang with no new analyst catalysts since
No new company-specific catalysts identified since Wednesday's close

New: Firefly completed a new ISO Class 8 cleanroom at its 144,000-sq-ft Cedar Park, Texas spacecraft campus, marked by a Sept 22, 2026 ribbon-cutting with Texas Space Commission, federal/state officials, and NASA program representatives -- a genuine new operational catalyst supporting spacecraft production capacity, confirmed via company press release and corroborated by multiple outlets (StockTitan, MarketBeat, Yahoo)

Existing catalysts unchanged: SSC Space contract for two Alpha launches from Esrange (Sept 9), Zeno Power Blue Ghost lunar-night radioisotope demo partnership, Elytra Deorbit System contract with the Defense Innovation Unit

BlueBird satellite constellation buildout continuing toward ~45 satellites targeted by early 2027 (previously disclosed, reiterated in a Sept 23 Motley Fool recap of the already-known July 2026 delay disclosure -- not a new catalyst)
$1.15B convertible bond raise (announced with the Q2 print) brought liquidity to ~$3.7B, cash runway a live investor debate but not a new development this run
Guggenheim raised PT to $57 (from $55) on Aug 27, 2026, maintaining Buy
Mizuho and Guggenheim both raised targets sharply in mid-August 2026 (to $42 and $55 respectively)

Recursion Pharmaceuticals data-license extension through November 2029 plus new RNA Foundation Model (TxFM) license announced Sept 21, 2026, confirmed via Tempus and Recursion press releases and an 8-K filing (agreements dated Sept 15, 2026) — a genuine incremental commercial catalyst, but it does not offset the insider-selling signal

CEO Eric Lefkofsky sold approximately $15.1M of stock via multiple S-SALE transactions on Sept 17, 2026 (187,558 shares across three filings at ~$80-81/share), filed Sept 18 — confirmed via SEC Form 4 data and cross-checked against Investing.com and MarketBeat reporting

FDA partial clinical hold on BHV-7000 (opakalim) new-patient enrollment issued Sept 4, 2026, remains open as of Sept 24 — confirmed via Biohaven's own 8-K/IR filing; hold applies only to new enrollment, dosing continues for 600+ already-randomized patients, and the fully-enrolled pivotal BHV7000-303 trial's H2 2026 topline data timeline is unaffected
SK Biopharmaceuticals Kv7-platform licensing deal (~$350M, announced in August) remains pending; HSR filing process was underway as of the Sept 10 update
FERC Docket EL26-101-000 (Oklo v. PJM) remains unresolved: PJM filed a Sept 18, 2026 motion opposing Oklo's Sept 14 answer; no FERC Commission order has been issued as of this run

PJM Interconnection Cycle 01 Phase I remains scheduled to begin September 28, 2026 (not yet occurred, not moved) -- Oklo's 750 MW hybrid project (150 MW nuclear + 300 MW gas + 300 MW fuel cells) remains excluded from the cycle pending FERC's ruling
Sept 22, 2026: Babcock and Arqit demonstrated a secure communications network designed to counter future quantum-enabled threats.
Sept 1, 2026: Arqit, Es'hailSat and AIEE demonstrated quantum-safe security across live satellite communications infrastructure.
